clue.text: Athlete has little time in store, say

indicators.note: one item placed in another means the store word wraps round the short time unit

parts.note: a store is a shop
T is the abbreviation for time
to say is to utter

explanation.surface: A sprinter with only minutes to spare goes shopping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Store, say' tempts as one unit, but the comma splits it: say is a separate verb that follows the store.
explanation.definitionFit: A shot-putter is a field-event competitor who hurls a heavy metal ball, so is one kind of athlete.

clue.text: Hurt with sharp tool, some hear

indicators.note: only some listeners will hear the match, since it depends on an accent that drops the r

parts.note: a saw is a toothed cutting tool

explanation.surface: Someone has been injured by a blade, and a few people overheard.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic accents such as standard British English, saw and sore sound the same; 'some' admits that others say them differently.
explanation.definitionFit: Sore means painful or aching, the condition of a hurt part of the body.

clue.text: Newgate's spirit of evil

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a former prison, so an ..., nick being slang for jail
second meaning: a familiar name for the Devil

explanation.walkthrough: Newgate was a notorious London prison, demolished in 1904; British slang calls a prison the nick, so Newgate is literally an old nick.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Nick is a traditional nickname for Satan, the personification of evil.

clue.text: Find a lovely partner to share a seasonal moment

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to attract, or pull, a gorgeous person, since cracker is slang for a stunner
second meaning: two people tugging a Christmas novelty until it bangs

explanation.walkthrough: In British slang to pull is to succeed in attracting someone, and a cracker is a very attractive person. A Christmas cracker is a paper tube pulled by two people at the festive table.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulling a Christmas cracker needs two people, one at each end, so it is a shared festive ritual.

clue.text: Company relocating to Peru

indicators.note: relocating means moving to a new place, so the letters are shifted into new positions

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A business announces a move to South America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Company' looks like a business; it is a band of performers.
explanation.definitionFit: A troupe is a company of actors, dancers or other performers who tour together.

clue.text: Sensing power certainly in crew

indicators.note: one thing being in another means the affirmative word sits inside the crew word

parts.note: a rowing eight is the crew of an eight-oared boat
yes is a firm certainly

explanation.surface: A crew definitely has a strong intuition among its members.
explanation.walkthrough: In rowing an eight is the whole crew of an eight-oared boat, a convention crosswords use often.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyesight is the faculty of vision, one of the senses, so a sensing power.

clue.text: International alliance British pass to the left

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for British

indicators.note: in an across clue, going to the left means reading the word from right to left

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass

explanation.surface: Talk of a treaty partnership in which Britain hands something on to the left.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloc is a group of countries joined by a common interest or treaty, an international alliance.

clue.text: Before entering parliament, brought up to watch one's words

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so the first piece is placed within the second
in a down clue, bringing something up means reading it from bottom to top

parts.note: the Dail is the lower house of the Irish parliament
pre- is the prefix meaning before

explanation.surface: A newly elected member is told to be careful what they say.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dail (Dáil Éireann) is Ireland's parliament. 'Watch one's words' looks like a warning to be careful; read literally it means watching speech on someone's lips.
explanation.definitionFit: To lip-read is to understand speech by observing the movements of a speaker's mouth.

clue.text: When horse perhaps barred from biting bird

parts.note: a biting wind is a cold one
a turkey is a bird

explanation.surface: A horse is kept away from snapping at a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: Horse is slang for heroin, and 'perhaps' marks it as one example of a drug; cutting someone off it abruptly is going cold turkey.
explanation.definitionFit: Cold turkey is sudden and complete withdrawal from an addictive drug, the state when heroin is stopped.

clue.text: Vigorous revolutionary initiated to war

parts.note: a red is a revolutionary communist
a soldier is blooded when given a first taste of battle

explanation.surface: A fiery radical gets a first experience of combat.
explanation.definitionFit: Red-blooded describes someone full of energy and spirit, a synonym for vigorous.

clue.text: Gem means nothing to friend

parts.note: O is the figure zero, nothing
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: Someone says a jewel is worthless when given to a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: An opal is an iridescent precious stone, so it is a gem.

clue.text: Repeats broadcast in the beginning appearing very different

indicators.note: one item sitting in another means the jumbled word goes inside the second

parts.note: the start is the beginning

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, as seed is, so the letters are spread into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Television reruns shown at launch look nothing like the originals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Repeats broadcast' reads as reruns on air, but repeats is only the raw letters, and the jumble is split open by the word for beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: Streets apart is an informal idiom for two things widely separated in nature or quality.

clue.text: Setback, the sack?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a letdown, a failure of hopes
second meaning, read cryptically: undoing someone's appointment to a post

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as DIS-APPOINTMENT: being given the sack un-appoints you. The question mark flags this playful split.
explanation.definitionFit: A disappointment is a setback to one's hopes, and a dismissal literally removes an appointment.

clue.text: Potential disaster of relations not all there?

parts.note: bananas is slang for crazy, not all there
kin are relations

explanation.surface: A family whose members are a little mad could spell trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces come in reverse order to the clue: BANANAS first, then KIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A banana skin is a slapstick hazard, hence any pitfall waiting to cause embarrassment or calamity.

clue.text: Financial institution initially lost a painter's capital

indicators.note: the institution's name loses whatever stands at its start, so its first letter goes

parts.note: a bank is a financial institution
taken as written
RA, Royal Academician, is the crossword painter

explanation.surface: A bank went bust and lost an artist's money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like money in this financial scene; it is a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Ankara has been the capital city of Turkey since 1923.

clue.text: Having abandoned love, words here failing to be more perceptive

indicators.note: words that fail break down and fall apart, so their letters are reassembled
something abandoned is left behind, so that letter is removed

parts.note: taken as written
love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: A jilted writer finds their words falter as they try to be sharper.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrewd means astute and sharp in judgement; the comparative form matches more perceptive.

clue.text: Where there's lots of the other fuels going up, Queen invested

definitions.text: Where there's lots of the other

indicators.note: invested means put into something, so the royal letters are placed inside
in a down clue, going up means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: oil and gas are two fuels
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword Queen

explanation.surface: Fuel prices rise and the monarch puts money into energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The other' is British slang for sex. ER goes inside the reversed fuels after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: A seraglio is a harem, the women's quarters of a sultan's palace, a place of much sexual activity.

clue.text: Married, 22, then died

parts.note: 22 across is built on the word case, and an attaché case is a slim briefcase
D is the abbreviation for died

explanation.surface: A terse register entry: wed, aged 22, and then dead.
explanation.walkthrough: The 22 looks like an age; it points to 22 across, AS THE CASE MAY BE, and the case wanted is an attaché case.
explanation.definitionFit: Attached is an informal way of saying someone is spoken for, in a relationship or wed.

clue.text: Over-fat, but eating to beat disease

indicators.note: eating means taking inside, so the second piece goes within the first
over means turned over, in a down clue flipped from bottom to top

parts.note: suet is hard animal fat
to tan someone's hide is to beat them

explanation.surface: An overweight patient keeps eating in the hope of fighting off an illness.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'Over-fat' hides that Over is a separate instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Tetanus is a bacterial infection causing muscle spasms, often called lockjaw, so it is a disease.

clue.text: Firm figure say hugs the bend

indicators.note: to hug is to wrap one's arms round, so the first word encloses the second

parts.note: to say is to state
a U-bend, the curved pipe under a sink

explanation.surface: A solid character hugs the curve, like a driver on a tight corner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like a company; with 'figure' it describes a solid sculpted figure. U goes inside STATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A statue is a carved or cast figure, made of solid stone or metal and so firm.

clue.text: Explorer brought over stuff of poisonous fumes — this!

definitions.text: Explorer brought over stuff of poisonous fumes — this!

indicators.note: brought over means turned over, so the explorer is read from bottom to top

parts.note: John Cabot, the Venetian-born explorer who sailed for England
CO is carbon monoxide, a poisonous gas

explanation.surface: An explorer brought back the leaf whose smoke is toxic, and here it is.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: explorers did bring this plant back from the Americas, and its smoke is poisonous.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobacco was brought to Europe from the New World by explorers, and burning it releases harmful smoke.

clue.text: Boy and girl in former Indian province

parts.note: Ben is a boy's name
gal is an informal word for a girl

explanation.surface: A young couple out in a region of the old Raj.
explanation.definitionFit: Bengal was a province of British India, partitioned in 1947 between India and what is now Bangladesh.

clue.text: Accordingly, open and shut?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: depending on the circumstances
second meaning, read cryptically: describing a case that is open and shut

explanation.walkthrough: An open-and-shut case is one with an obvious outcome, so 'open and shut' describes the kind of case it may be; the question mark flags the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means according to the circumstances, which is what accordingly conveys in such use.

clue.text: Marks deducted from right exam

indicators.note: something deducted is subtracted, so that letter is taken away from the following word

parts.note: moral means right, ethically sound
M is the abbreviation for mark, the old German currency

explanation.surface: An examiner docks points from a correct test answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marks' looks like exam scores; it is the German currency.
explanation.definitionFit: An oral is a spoken examination, as in language tests, so it is an exam.

clue.text: Obliging sort

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a type or variety

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one phrase about a helpful person; the two words are separate meanings of one short word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective for helpful, generous behaviour and a noun meaning a class or type.

clue.text: Sign about free gold seen by one not peeas lightly!

indicators.note: about means placed round something, so the sign wraps the other letters

parts.note: Cancer is a sign of the zodiac

indicators.note: letters set free are released from their order and can rearrange

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A star sign and loose gold watched by someone heavy on their feet.
explanation.walkthrough: The word printed as 'peeas' is garbled in the source; the sense is someone who does not step lightly, since clogs are noisy wooden shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: A clog dancer wears wooden-soled shoes and dances noisily, beating out rhythms rather than treading softly.

clue.text: Settle into one's tree

indicators.note: into means looking inside the following words, where the answer sits across the gap

parts.note: letters running from the end of one's into the start of tree

explanation.surface: Someone makes themselves at home up in their tree.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a bird at home, which suits the answer, but the letters are concealed across the apostrophe and the word break.
explanation.definitionFit: To nest is to settle into a home, as a bird does when it builds its nest.

clue.text: Poet's written about dwarf feature of the smallest room

indicators.note: written about here means written the other way round, from back to front

parts.note: T S Eliot, the poet
a troll is a dwarf or giant of Scandinavian folklore

explanation.surface: A verse writer has composed something about a little person found in the lavatory.
explanation.walkthrough: The smallest room is a British euphemism for the toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: A toilet roll hangs in every lavatory, so it is a fixture of the smallest room.
